title: Machine learning derives a CSF YWHAG:NPTX2 ratio for cognitive decline in Alzheimer's
summary: CSF proteomics in 3,397 individuals from six prospective Alzheimer's disease cohorts found synapse proteins to be the strongest correlates of cognitive impairment, independent of amyloid and tau. Machine learning derived the CSF YWHAG:NPTX2 ratio, which explained 27% of the variance in cognitive impairment beyond CSF pTau181:Abeta42 in A+T1+ individuals. It predicted conversion from cognitively normal to mild cognitive impairment (hazard ratio 3.0) and from mild cognitive impairment to dementia (hazard ratio 2.2) over 15 years, and a plasma proteomic signature evaluated in 13,401 samples partly recapitulated the ratio. This is an observational biomarker study.
ai_technology: Machine learning on CSF proteomic data to derive a synaptic protein ratio biomarker

evidence.tested: Association and prognostic analyses across six cohorts with plasma proteomic replication in 13,401 samples.
evidence.unknown: Causality and use in clinical practice; the plasma signature only partly recapitulated the CSF ratio; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning selected the YWHAG:NPTX2 ratio from proteomic data.
